newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures up, look set for more gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures up, look set for more gains.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures firmed on Tuesday and appeared to be getting ready to break up out of their recent trading range, dealers said.

The December Nikkei futures contract closed at 21,210 points, up 115 points, after reaching an earlier high of 21,300, the top of the recent well-established trading band between 20,750 and 21,300 points.

"Technically, I believe the market is trying to go higher," said one Singapore futures dealer. "And people seem to be hungry, waiting for some good news that will pop the contract up into higher territory."
"Unless New York corrects downwards, it shouldn't come down," said another dealer.
Dealers said the generally bullish sentiment had been reinforced by a positive reaction to the latest report and briefing by Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA).
The November EPA report said the Japanese economy was recovering slowly and played down potential investor worries.
At a subsequent news conference, EPA Minister Taro Aso said: "It is desirable for the Bank of Japan to maintain its easy credit policy for the time being."
"The report did no harm. That makes me think the market could go higher from here," said one dealer.
Chart analysts said the immediate target for the December Nikkei futures contract was 21,300 points. If it broke through that barrier, it might jump several hundred points.
"The second target would be 21,850 points -- clear of resistance between 21,500 and 21,750," said a chart analyst. "If it breaks through there it will swing up to 22,000."
